lesson.menu_desc: The first ninety seconds of a prospect call -- 26 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 1 -- Who's on the Call?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fábia | Lesson 1 -- Who's on the Call?

listenings.text: Hi Fabia, it's Karen Whitfield. Just a quick message before Tuesday. I've invited one person from each area, so there will be five of us on the call. I hope that is not too many. What I would really like to cover first is payroll, because that is where we have had problems with our current provider, and honestly it is the reason we are talking to you at all. The rest can wait. Oh, and could you send a short agenda before the call? With five people, I would rather nobody talked over anybody. Thanks. See you Tuesday.

Right, two minutes before you go in. This one came through the website, and one of our current clients referred them, so they already trust us a little. Use that. There are two names on the invite, but be ready: with these companies more people usually join at the last minute, and nobody introduces themselves. So in the first minute, ask each person to say their name and their area, and write it down. Half of them will be there just to listen. And they will ask about price early. Do not answer that before you know what they actually need. Good luck.

bank.label: Keep these open on your second screen
items: Before we start, could I ask who's joining us today?
And which area do you look after?
We're a BPO firm — we handle payroll, finance and tax.
We specialise in outsourcing, not in consulting.
May I ask who the decision-maker is on your side?
Who should I direct that to?
Let me make sure I understood you correctly.
Shall we agree on an agenda before we start?

the money a company pays its staff
all the clients one firm looks after
anyone with an interest in the decision
the person who can say yes or no

items.situation: Ten people join the call and only two were on the invite. Say your opening line.
tips: Before we start, could I ask ...?
And which area do you look after?

items.situation: A prospect asks what your firm does. Answer in three sentences, no more.
You have been talking for twenty minutes and still do not know who signs the contract. Ask.
tips: Who should I direct that to?
Is there anyone else who needs to approve this?

items.situation: The prospect says something long and you lose the thread halfway. Do not go quiet.
tips: Let me make sure I understood you correctly.
Could you say a bit more about that?

items.situation: They open with "just send us your rates". You do not know what they need yet.
tips: Of course. Before I do, could I ask ...?
It depends on what you'd like us to handle.

casebank.label: Useful language
items: What made you look for a partner now?
Who handles that for you today?
What worries you most about outsourcing?
It depends on what you'd like us to handle.
I'd rather understand the problem first.
That's not something we specialise in.
I don't think we're the right fit, and here's why.
Would it help if I put that in writing?
Let me come back to you on that.
Shall we agree on an agenda first?
